properties.name: record_change deliberately dates nothing because "the epoch places it in time" — and 212 of 214 epochs carry no calendar date, so the placement is ordinal, not temporal
properties.statement:
FOUND WHILE DOGFOODING the F-06 fix, 2026-09-10 — the session went to record its own three fixes with both a date and a repair disposition and could not.

THE SURFACE SPLITS THE TWO FIELDS AND NEITHER TOOL HAS BOTH:
  `add_change_event`  has `detected_at`, has NO `repair` / `stands_in_for`
  `record_change`     has `repair` / `stands_in_for`, has NO `detected_at`
So a repair recorded through the discipline `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed` points at is UNDATED BY CONSTRUCTION, and a dated event cannot say whether it reached its cause.

⭐ THE OMISSION IS DELIBERATE AND REASONED, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A BUG. temporal.rs states it in the call itself: *"`record_change` pins the event to an EPOCH, which is this path's way of placing it in time; it carries no calendar date of its own to pass on, and inventing one would be a claim nobody made."* That argument is sound and consistent with `req:defaults-do-not-assert`.

⚠️ BUT IT RESTS ON AN ASSUMPTION THAT DOES NOT HOLD ON THIS GRAPH. Measured 2026-09-10:
    DesignEpochs                                    214
    carrying any calendar date (created_at/at/date)   2
    ChangeEvents                                    907
    without detected_at                             519
An epoch places an event in a SEQUENCE, not on a CALENDAR. So "the epoch places it in time" is true ordinally and false temporally, and the comparison the date exists for — ordering a change against a check's `last_run_at`, which IS a calendar date — cannot be made for anything recorded through this path.

NOT A PROPOSAL, and deliberately not fixed here. Three routes exist and they are different design choices, not one obvious repair: give `record_change` a `detected_at` (contradicting a documented decision), make `add_epoch` write a date so the epoch really does place things in time, or accept that repairs are ordinally placed and stop claiming otherwise in the comment. The last is free and the first two are not.

📌 THIS ALSO BOUNDS THE F-06 FIX SHIPPED THE SAME DAY. The `undated` note was added to `add_change_event`, which is the tool that HAS the field and the one hxm_program was using. `record_change` is untouched and still cannot be dated at all — so the fix reaches the reported path and not this one, which is correct scoping rather than an oversight, and is written here so nobody reads F-06 as fully closed.
